full_judgment:
3. The plaintiff-respondent filed the suit in respect of the schedule 'A' of the plaint stating, inter alia, that the suit land was khas land of the Government and the same was leased out to the petitioners by the then Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Rajshahi, permanently on receipt of 'premium in Naogaon Settlement Case No.2325 of 1968-69. The possession of the suit land was duly handed over to the petitioner and a Kabuliyat was executed and registered on 28.11.1977. Although in the comment column of C.S. and S.A. Khatian of the suit property it was mentioned as "Peer's Dargabari" but, in fact, since long there has been no such Dargabari in the suit property and no religious rites and ceremonies were performed in the suit property and the said land has been in continuous use as a cultivable land and the plaintiff since his lease has been possessing and enjoying the suit property by cultivating paddy and other crops therein. Recently local enemical persons, the defendant Nos.4- 7 filed an objection to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon for cancellation of the permanent settlement of the plaintiff stating that the suit land is a religious property. The said objection has been registered as Miscellaneous Case No.2/X111/198-82 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon wherein the C.O. (Revenue), Neamatpur was directed to submit a spot inquiry report of the suit property. The C.O. (Revenue), Neamatpur submitted his report mentioning that the suit property was not a religious property and it is cultivable land. But. without considering the said report Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon, cancelled the permanent settlement of the plaintiff through order dated 30.10.1984. The plaintiff, thereafter, preferred an appeal before the Divisional Commissioner Rajshahi who affirmed the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon, by his order dated 04.11.1989. The further case of the plaintiff is that he did not violate. any of the terms and conditions of the lease deed of the permanent settlement and was competent under the law when he obtained the lease as he had not more than 2.30 acres of land. 

 4. The defendant Nos.1 and 2-4 contested the suit by filing separate written statement alleging, inter alia, that in the C.S. and Khatian the suit land was recorded as "Peer's Dargabari" and the same was used for religious purpose. The plaintiff by suppressing fact of the actual nature and feature of the suit property obtained the lease from the office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Rajshahi. The plaintiff earlier filed Other Class Suit concerning suit land which was withdrawn and he also filed a C.R. case against the contesting  defendant under Section 379 of the Penal Code which was also dismissed. The defendant on knowing the lease of the petitioner filed objection before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon, being satisfied cancelled the lease of the plaintiff lawfully. The legal formalities for granting lease since not being followed while granting the permanent settlement in favour of the petitioner, the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Rajshahi, correctly dismissed the appeal preferred by the plaintiff against his cancellation of the lease. The further case of the defendant is that the plaintiff is not entitled to get relief because he is not a professional cultivator and he lives in Rajshahi town far from the suit property. Hence he prayed for the dismissal of the suit. 

 6. Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-record, appearing for the respondent No. I submits that in view of the recording of the suit land in the name of the plaintiff although mentioned in the comment column that the same having been recorded as "Peerer Dargabari" but has no basis inasmuch as nothing has been produced to show that it was "Peerer Dargabari". It appears that there is no existence of "Peerer .Dargabari" and as such, the comment in the comment column of a Khatian has not been recorded at the time of recording of the recent Khatian as the same has no basis. Moreso, the subsequent Khatians are silent of the above comment but simply recorded in the name of plaintiff's predecessors. In that view of the matter the Courts of appeal below proceeded and dismissed the appeal which was not maintainable in law. 

 9. Further, though the previous Khatian of the land was recorded to be "Peer's Dargabari" but the land at present appears to be nal land duly cultivated by the plaintiff. The nature and character of the suit land having been changed and the Government also treated the same as cultivable land and considering the true state of affairs leased. out the same to the plaintiff on permanent basis.
